item.title: Mathematics of Herding
item.description: arXiv:2610.23992v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A herd of animals often follows a leader who sets the direction of travel. The leader sometimes turns unexpectedly and the followers reshuffle. Yet the herd regroups itself and stays coherent. Our work aims to understand the herding behavior mathematically. We construct a minimal discrete-time nonequilibrium dynamical system with one-way coupling, and the minimal structure allows an exact analysis. Take the location of each follower in the frame of the leader. The recorded locations form a distribution. The limit of the distribution is the asymptotic spatial measure, whose geometric representation we study. The dynamics of the herd have an exact operator representation with two factors, the operator of a fixed leader-follower pair and the operator of the interaction rules, which reshuffle the pairs. We show that the influence of the leader passes through some follower more than once. As a result, two followers can have reciprocal influence, despite the one-way coupling.
item.dc:creator: Sayomi Kamimoto

item.title: Extinction and the global structure of positive equilibria in a ratio-dependent intraguild predation model
item.description: arXiv:2610.23995v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study an intraguild predation model with ratio-dependent trophic interactions. We first derive sufficient conditions for consumer extinction, total extinction, and global convergence to biologically relevant boundary equilibria. We then turn to coexistence at equilibrium and introduce a biologically motivated coordinate transformation that reduces the positive-equilibrium problem to an explicitly parameterized one-dimensional curve. This reduction enables us to determine how the positive-equilibrium branch connects to boundary equilibria and to classify all of its admissible global geometries. We also discuss the stability of positive equilibria. Numerical examples suggest the presence of periodic and chaotic coexistence, as well as several forms of multiple attractors.
item.dc:creator: Tzu-Hsuan Chan, Chang-Hong Wu

item.title: Singular Aubry--Mather Sets for a Homogeneous Single-Input Control System
item.description: arXiv:2610.24145v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop an Aubry--Mather theory for the abnormal arcs of a time-minimal single-input affine control system in dimension three with homogeneous cubic drift. We show that the Bonnard--Kupka semi-invariant defining the abnormal locus is a Darboux polynomial of the desingularized singular field, with an explicit cofactor; this gives the invariance of the abnormal locus, a closed formula for the multiplier of its periodic components and, through the antipodal symmetry of the model, their description as lifts of ovals of a real plane quintic. For a compact invariant set of a singular flow we then define a singular Aubry--Mather structure, whose Lagrangian is supported on the graph of the singular field and whose Hamilton--Jacobi equation is linear in the momentum. We prove a duality formula for the critical value, the existence of critical subsolutions strict outside the Aubry set, and the covariance of the structure under time changes. On the abnormal locus the structure selects the periodic components of minimal average cost, governs transverse stability, and exhibits a sharp obstruction to correctors along heteroclinic cycles; for the radial exponent of the homogeneous dynamics, the corrector is the periodic part of the logarithmic radius. An explicit cubic example illustrates the results.
item.dc:creator: Bernard Bonnard, Cristian Mendico

item.title: Geometric Stability of Dynamical Systems with Self-Generated State-Space Memory
item.description: arXiv:2610.24152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a geometric stability framework for dynamical systems coupled to memory fields generated by their own state trajectories. Temporal age and state-space displacement enter a nonlinear hereditary force admitting an exact, trajectory-dependent velocity representation. A common velocity-history phase space contains both resting and uniformly translating solutions. We establish global velocity arrest under a uniform geometric memory-gain bound and obtain exact translating-speed balance laws from the full radial imprint. The response slope yields a positive longitudinal exponent on rising-speed branches, while a complementary contraction criterion gives local exponential attraction to selected descending branches in the scalar velocity dynamics, in fading-memory topology. Our principal result is a constructive geometric non-identifiability theorem: two systems with identical nonlinear force operators on an open neighborhood of rest can exhibit sharply different complete-motion behavior at the same subcritical gain. In the first, every admissible trajectory with bounded velocity prehistory comes to rest exponentially; in the second, locally attracting rest coexists with a locally attracting translating branch and an additional spectrally unstable translating branch. The infinite-memory case exhibits exponentially flat force differences, with all finite-order equilibrium derivatives agreeing despite the possibility of distinct global translating families. The framework also yields classical Volterra kernels and distributed-derivative transfer functions by linearization.
item.dc:creator: Robert Vrabel

item.title: Global stability of Michaelis-Menten networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.24351v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a very nice paper, Blanchini, Breda, Giordano and Liessi studied networks of species coupled through Michaelis-Menten interactions. Under standard assumptions of strong connectedness and non-degeneracy, they show that there is a unique equilibrium, which is (locally) asymptotically stable. This note shows that global stability, which was stated there as an open problem, holds as well. In fact, whenever a positive equilibrium exists, it attracts every solution with positive initial condition, with no connectedness or non-degeneracy hypothesis at all; those assumptions are needed only in order to guarantee existence and to cover solutions starting on the boundary of the orthant. The key is to note that the system is contractive with respect to the Thompson part metric.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo D. Sontag

item.title: Asymptotics for the number of saddle connections on a slit torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.24429v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider a flat torus with a marked line segment $\beta$ and prove linear asymptotics for closed curves on the torus disjoint from the interior of the line segment. We also consider segments that begin and terminate at the end points of $\beta$ whose interiors are disjoint from $\beta$ and prove $L\log L$ asymptotics. In all cases, after quotienting by the growth rate, we compute the constant explicitly, which differs depending on whether or not $\beta$ lies in a periodic direction on the torus. In particular, when $\beta$ lies along a non-periodic trajectory, we show the constant is $2/(|\beta| \zeta(2))$. Moreover, we prove that as a function of the holonomy vector of $\beta$, the constants are continuous at the points where $\beta$ lies in a non-periodic direction.
item.dc:creator: David Aulicino, Howard Masur

item.title: A new class of pyramidal central configurations for spatial Newtonian 6-body problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.24445v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While a non-concyclic rhombus can support a central configuration in the planar Newtonian four-body problem, such a configuration cannot serve as the base of a pyramidal central configuration in the spatial five-body problem. In this paper, we establish the existence of a new class of pyramidal central configurations in the spatial Newtonian six-body problem, characterized by a non-concyclic quadrilateral base. This geometric structure distinguishes the new configurations from the known pyramidal central configurations of the spatial five-body problem. We investigate several fundamental properties of these configurations and provide numerical examples illustrating the theoretical results in each case. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this new class of central configurations can be used to construct perverse solutions in three-dimensional space, revealing an additional connection between the geometry of central configurations and the dynamics of the Newtonian $N$-body problem.
item.dc:creator: Liang Ding, Jin Wang, Jinrong Wang, Zhifu Xie

item.title: Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on tori isotopic to Anosov linear maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be an Anosov diffeomorphism on the $d$-torus which is strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center. If $d=3$ or if $f$ is isotopic to its linear part, where the isotopy is contained in the set of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms, we construct systems of strong-unstable and center-stable Margulis measures which are holonomy invariant. As a consequence, we obtain a characterization of measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along strong-unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the unstable topological entropy, a measure of maximal unstable entropy and the Margulis system can be retrieved from the Pollicott-Ruelle spectrum of $f$.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Humbert

item.title: Analytical Methods for Solving Non-Autonomous Higher-Order Nonlinear Difference Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.24657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A system of four-dimensional fifth-order rational difference equations with variable coefficients is considered. The method employed is the well-known Lie symmetry analysis initially developed for differential equations. Linearised symmetry conditions are applied, reduction operators are introduced, functional equations are solved, and symmetry generators are derived. The admitted point symmetries are then used to construct closed-form solutions. This work is a non-autonomous generalisation of autonomous fifth-order rational systems in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Tshifhiwa Murovhi, Mensah Folly-Gbetoula, Kwassi Anani

item.title: Physical measures for partially hyperbolic systems with $u$-definite subbundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.24743v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study \(C^{1+\alpha}\) diffeomorphisms of a compact Riemannian manifold \(\mathbf{M}\) with an attracting set \(\Lambda\) admitting a partially hyperbolic splitting \[ T_\Lambda \mathbf{M} = E^u\oplus C_1\oplus\cdots\oplus C_k\oplus E^s. \] We assume that, for every ergodic Gibbs \(u\)-state supported on \(\Lambda\), the Lyapunov exponents along each \(C_i\) are either all positive or all negative. We prove that \(\Lambda\) supports finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures whose basins cover Lebesgue almost every point of its topological basin. Our approach relies on an empirical basin-covering theorem for attracting sets with dominated splittings. Its proof hinges on a new notion of sliding suffix times, which allows us to synchronize expansion and contraction along a common empirical subsequence.
item.dc:creator: Yongluo Cao, Zeya Mi

item.title: Interior caustics and rigidity near noncircular ellipses
item.description: arXiv:2610.24848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove local rigidity near every fixed noncircular ellipse from integrable rational caustics in an arbitrary nonempty open rotation interval $I\subset(0,1/2)$. For each fixed $r>11/2$ and bound on the $H^r$ norm of the elliptic graph displacement, every sufficiently $C^1$-small positively curved perturbation admitting such caustics at all rational rotations in $I$ is an ellipse. A fixed $C^6$ bound may replace the Sobolev bound, with $C^1$ smallness retained. The caustic hypothesis can be restricted to a suitably chosen sequence of rational rotations in $I$ with any prescribed rational $\rho_*\in I$ as its unique accumulation point, together with finitely many supplementary rotations in $I$; this family depends only on the reference ellipse, interval, and anchor. The main linear result classifies all real $L^2$ displacements satisfying the constant rational orbit-sum equations throughout $I$ as infinitesimal ellipse deformations, and establishes their analyticity and rational continuation in the complexified boundary parameter. The proof combines analytic continuation and elimination of monodromy with quantitative caustic estimates, finite detection, and Fourier interpolation.
item.dc:creator: Guan HUANG

item.title: Stable Ergodicity for Expanding on Average Partially Hyperbolic Diffeomorphisms with Two-Dimensional Center
item.description: arXiv:2610.24946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study a property called expansion on average (EA) defined for any partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism satisfying an unstable center bunching condition. Under a mild set of assumptions, we show that the EA property implies $C^2$-stable ergodicity with respect to volume. Our theorem applies to any conservative, $u$-center bunched, robustly dynamically coherent, partially hyperbolic $C^2$-diffeomorphism with two-dimensional center and one-dimensional unstable bundle, whose action on $E^c$ is close to conservative. We do not assume that the center leaves are compact or that the center foliation has a fibration structure. Our mechanism for ergodicity also does not use accessibility or the existence of a dominated splitting in $E^c$. The EA property is inspired by a condition with the same name defined for IID random dynamical systems on surfaces, and our proofs extend ideas from that setting. The EA property is systematically studied in very recent work of Carrasco-Obata-Saghin-Yang, where they obtain continuity of center Lyapunov exponents, strong positive recurrence, and existence of finitely many SRB measures. With input from our result, they obtain uniqueness of SRB measures for dissipative perturbations of certain EA diffeomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Ben Cooper

item.title: Bounded orbits on homogeneous spaces and bounded geodesics on locally symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.24979v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present a unified approach to proving the following two results: (i) Let $G$ be a Lie group, $\Gamma$ a lattice in $G$, $X=G/\Gamma$, and let $F$ be a one-parameter $\mathrm{Ad}$-diagonalizable subgroup of $G$. Then the set $$ \{x\in X:Fx\text{ is bounded in }X\} $$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $X$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 7.1]{AGK} of An-Guan-Kleinbock in 2015. (ii) Let $G$ be a connected semisimple Lie group with finite center and without compact factors, $K\leq G$ a maximal compact subgroup, $\Gamma\leq G$ a torsion-free lattice, and $M=K\backslash G/\Gamma$. Then for any $p\in M$, the set $$\{\xi\in S_pM:\gamma(p,\xi)\text{ is bounded in }M\}$$ is hyperplane absolute winning on $S_pM$, where $\gamma(p,\xi)$ denotes the geodesic ray through the base point $p$ in the direction $\xi$. This fully solves a conjecture [Conjecture 1.2]{GW26} of Guan-Wu in 2026.
item.dc:creator: Chengyang Wu

item.title: Exponential loss of memory for random Lasota--Yorke convex maps with local average expansion
item.description: arXiv:2610.25037v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study i.i.d. random compositions of piecewise convex interval maps whose first branch is full. Uniform expansion is not required, and the maps may have contracting branches. Under a local average expansion condition at the origin, we prove both quenched and annealed exponential loss of memory for initial densities of bounded variation. The proof is based on a coupling argument. As applications, we obtain the quenched almost sure invariance principle and a rate of convergence in the quenched central limit theorem.
item.dc:creator: Hongfei Cui, Juho Lepp\"{a}nen

item.title: Moser Regularization of the CR3BP for Symmetric Orbits: Bifurcation Networks of Lunar Orbits
item.description: arXiv:2610.25042v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We develop a computational framework based on Moser regularization for the analysis of symmetric periodic orbits in the spatial Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP). The formulation enables the numerical continuation of periodic orbit families through collision with either primary, together with the computation of Floquet multipliers and stability indices entirely in regularized coordinates. We further provide a characterization and numerical detection scheme for symmetric periodic collision orbits. We apply this framework to the Earth-Moon CR3BP and uncover bifurcation networks connecting several classical lunar periodic orbit families. Higher-period vertical bifurcations of the planar $L_1$ Lyapunov family generate spatial bridges reconnecting different regions of the same family across its collision with the Earth, while corresponding bifurcations of the $L_2$ Lyapunov family form bridges to planar families associated with retrograde comet orbits. Furthermore, period-multiplying bifurcations of Near-Rectilinear Halo Orbit (NRHO) families produce a systematic network connecting to planar prograde and retrograde families. These bifurcation connections in the near-Moon dynamics retain the characteristic organization by covering multiplicities of the corresponding bifurcation network in the limiting Hill problem. Conley-Zehnder indices and related symplectic invariants complement the numerical continuation and provide a topological organization of the results.
item.dc:creator: Cengiz Aydin, Chankyu Joung

item.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
item.description: arXiv:2610.25253v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $\pi_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.
item.dc:creator: Huagui Duan, Hui Liu, Wei Wang

item.title: A coupling normal form for reversible center-center Hamiltonians with application to the restricted three-body problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.25355v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Near a reversible center--center equilibrium, the Birkhoff normal form does not describe the families bifurcating from the continued tori, while resonant normal forms capture these bifurcations through a reduced system. For such equilibria with a reflection symmetry, we develop a coupling normal form in which the bifurcating families also appear as tori of action normal forms. Along a selected coupling direction, the first slow harmonic is absorbed into an action-dependent counterterm. We prove that the coupled recursion determines unique even counterterm coefficients, a formal action normal form, and an exact counterterm factorization. The factorization gives a scalar recovery constraint, whose trivial factor corresponds to the Birkhoff normal form. At every finite order, a symmetric pair of bifurcating branches leaves the trivial branch at a critical curve and carries approximately invariant tori and circles with explicit residual estimates. Applied to the spatial circular restricted three-body problem, the construction yields approximate halo orbits and quasi-halo tori.
item.dc:creator: Mingpei Lin

item.title: Equidistribution, multipliers, and moving targets in polynomial families
item.description: arXiv:2610.25509v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study equidistribution of parameters for each of which a polynomial has a cycle with a prescribed moving multiplier in the full critically marked or unicritical polynomial families of a given degree $d>1$. For the full critically marked monic polynomial family $f=(f_\lambda)$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$, of degree $d$, letting $p_{f,n}^*(\lambda,w)$ be the multiplier polynomial for cycles of formal exact period $n$ having multiplier $w$, we show that for any target sequence $w_n=d^na_n$ satisfying $n^{-1}\log|a_n|\to\ell\in[-\infty,+\infty)$, the averaged current of integration $\nu(n)^{-1}[p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)=0]$ along the zero divisor of $p_{f,n}^*(\cdot,w_n)$ tends to the $(1,1)$-current $\mathrm{d}\mathrm{d}^c\max\{L_d,\log d+\ell\}$ in the sense of currents on $\mathbb{C}^{d-1}$ as $n\to\infty$, where $L_d$ is the Lyapunov exponent function and $\nu(n)$ is the degree of the $n$th formal exact dynatomic polynomial associated to $f$. We also obtain the corresponding equidistribution theorem for the unicritical family $f_\lambda(z)=z^d+\lambda$, $\lambda\in\mathbb{C}$, of degree $d$. The proof combines thermodynamic formalism, the Eremenko--Levin multiplier bound, and a comparison principle for plurisubharmonic functions, in a partly quantitative manner. A key ingredient is the vanishing of the bifurcation measure on the boundary of every component of the interior of the connectedness locus for the full critically marked family, which we show using Kiwi's study of critical portraits and rational laminations.
item.dc:creator: Y\^usuke Okuyama

item.title: Expanding on Average Diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2610.25559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the statistical properties of partially hyperbolic diffeomorphisms with a two-dimensional center exhibiting mixed behavior, without assuming a dominated splitting inside the center. We introduce the notion of an expanding on average for partially hyperbolic diffeomorphism and, under a center jacobian assumption, we prove the existence of finitely many ergodic hyperbolic SRB measures, and show the strong positive recurrence property, which implies that each SRB measure, up to a period, satisfies exponential decay of correlations, among other strong statistical laws. We apply our results to several examples.
item.dc:creator: Pablo D. Carrasco, Davi Obata, Radu Saghin, Jiagang Yang

item.title: On the Hausdorff dimension of oscillatory motions in three-body problems
item.description: arXiv:2610.25750v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that for the Sitnikov example and for the restricted planar circular 3-body problem the set of oscillatory motions often has maximal Hausdorff dimension. Also, we construct Newhouse domains for both problems.
item.dc:creator: Anton Gorodetski, Vadim Kaloshin

item.title: When vector abundance constrains vector-borne transmission: inside epidemic dynamics within a prescribed population
item.description: arXiv:2610.25971v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The global burden of vector-borne diseases continues to rise, presenting escalating challenges to public health and agricultural systems. Their expanding geographic range and associated impacts underscore the need for tools to project disease dynamics and evaluate interventions. Mechanistic compartmental host--vector models provide such a framework by explicitly representing transmission processes. However, while these models often couple vector population dynamics with infection spread, the inherent complexity of vector demographic processes calls for a more modular approach. In this study, we consider the setting in which the total vector abundance is an externally-prescribed input to a general vector-mediated transmission model. Our objectives are threefold: (i) to provide theoretical guarantees for ensuring consistency between the prescribed total vector abundance and the dynamics of the model compartments, (ii) to characterize model properties related to the local reproduction index (informing extinction or emergence near the time of introduction) and the inter-seasonal propagation, and (iii) to derive insights for diseases transmitted by Aedes albopictus in mainland France. We apply this framework by feeding the epidemiological model with vector-abundance data obtained either from entomological surveillance systems or from an external detailed population dynamic model. Moreover, epidemiological national surveillance data are used to estimate the transmission parameter. Based on this, we derive conditions for emergence and extinction, and show how the extent of the epidemic depends on introduction timing, transmission rate, and susceptible population density. Taken together, these results highlight the value of generating and leveraging entomological surveillance data as well as their model-based counterparts when observations are unavailable (which is particularly relevant in the context of global warming and for the evaluation of vector-control strategies). Overall, we establish a refined framework integrating such data or forecast into compartmental models, with strong potential for a wide range of applications in animal, human or plant health.
item.dc:creator: Lise Isnel (BioSP), Julien Papa{\"i}x (BioSP), Olivier Bonnefon (BioSP), Samuel Soubeyrand (BioSP), Lionel Roques (BioSP)

item.title: Complex Analytic Structure of Hybrid Classes of Generalized Polynomial-like Mappings
item.description: arXiv:2610.25983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study hybrid classes of generalized polynomial-like mappings. We show that locally they are complex analytic submanifolds with finite codimension equal to the total order of critical points in the filled Julia set (counting multiplicity).
item.dc:creator: Miaokeyan Lin, Weixiao Shen, Yimin Wang

item.title: Bernoulli property for skew products of exponentially mixing systems over Anosov bases
item.description: arXiv:2610.26018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study $C^{1+\beta}$ skew products over topologically mixing Anosov diffeomorphisms, with fiber dynamics generated by a locally free $\mathbb{R}^k$-action. For a Gibbs measure on the base and a cocycle with a nonzero average, we establish a Bernoulli criterion for ergodic invariant product measures. The fiber hypotheses apply to actions that are exponentially mixing with respect to the SRB measure, as well as volume measures that are almost exponentially mixing with a limit SRB measure. As an application, when the fibers are generated by geodesic flows or Weyl chamber actions, our results reveal a statistical phase transition determined by the drift.
item.dc:creator: Changguang Dong, Qiujie Qiao

item.title: Local structure of sumsets and projections of self-affine carpets
item.description: arXiv:2610.26119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that if $X$ and $Y$ are self-similar sets in $\mathbb{R}$ with multiplicatively independent contraction ratios, then the Assouad dimension of $X+Y$ is one. As an application, we show that for a large class of self-affine carpets, the Assouad dimension of any non-principal orthogonal projection is one. The latter result is new even for the simplest case of Bedford-McMullen carpets.
item.dc:creator: Roope Anttila, Jonathan M. Fraser

item.title: $L^p$-Khinchin sequences and transference principles
item.description: arXiv:2610.26152v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A sequence \((\lambda_n)_{n\ge1}\) of distinct positive integers is called an \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequence, where $1\le p\le\infty$, if $ n^{-1}\sum_{k=1}^n f(\lambda_k x) \longrightarrow \int_{\mathbb T}f\,d\mathfrak m $ a.e. $x\in\mathbb T$ for every \(f\in L^p(\mathbb T)\). When $1\le p<\infty$, we characterize the \(L^p\)-Khinchin sequences by a weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality for the associated averaging operators. We also establish a transference principle reducing the weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequality to weak $(p,p)$ maximal inequalities for three model systems: translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the semigroup $\mathbb{N}_0$, translation along a lattice path in the infinite direct sum of the group $\mathbb{Z}$ and translation on the circle $\mathbb{T}$. As consequences, we prove that $(2^n+1)_{n\ge1}$, the Fibonacci sequence, sequences of distinct primes and their partial products are \emph{not} $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We study the special class of multiplicative sequences generated by infinite words and we show that balanced infinite words generate $L^1$-Khinchin sequences, while typical random multiplicative sequences over at least two coprime integers are almost surely not $L^p$-Khinchin for any $1\le p<\infty$. We also obtain a {Conze-type principle} for countably generated semigroup actions on a probability space.
item.dc:creator: Aihua Fan, Shilei Fan, Tongjin Li

item.title: Input-to-Output Stability and Consensus Control of Opinion Dynamics on Graph State-Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.26224v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes a modeling of opinion dynamics in social systems with evolving structures on the Graph State-Space. It builds upon the Hegselmann-Krause (HK) model with variable influence weights, integrated into a hybrid dynamical systems framework where structural changes (agent addition/removal) are induced by inputs. We establish an Inputto-Output Stability (IOS) result under a strong connectivity assumption, using a nonsmooth Lyapunov function based on the opinion diameter; we show that the consensus expansion is then bounded by the maximal deviation of incoming agents relative to the existing convex hull. Assuming constant influence weights, we propose a consensus control result via agent injection in the social system. The results of this paper initiate, to the best of our knowledge, the analysis of resilience, stability, and control of dynamic systems on Graph State-Space.
item.dc:creator: Arthur Doliveira (DIAPRO), Christophe Roman (DIAPRO), Guillaume Graton (DIAPRO), Mustapha Ouladsine

item.title: Entropy and periodic points in pseudo-Anosov isotopy classes
item.description: arXiv:2610.26230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $f$ be a pseudo-Anosov homeomorphism of a closed orientable surface of genus at least two. We prove that, for every $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $g$ isotopic to $f$, the exponential growth rate of the number of nonempty Nielsen classes of its iterates equals $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)$ if and only if $h_{\mathrm{top}}(g)=h_{\mathrm{top}}(f)$. Thus Nielsen growth captures the full entropy precisely for representatives minimizing entropy in their isotopy class. For $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphisms, $\alpha>0$, we identify this growth rate with the entropy of the global orbit quotient in Fathi's hyperbolic extension and establish Bowen's periodic-point formula for the quotient. We also prove that quotient entropy is upper semicontinuous in the $C^0$ topology throughout the isotopy class and continuous at every $C^{1+\alpha}$ diffeomorphism, even under perturbations by arbitrary homeomorphisms in the class.
item.dc:creator: Pablo D. Carrasco, Federico Rodriguez-Hertz, Jana Rodriguez-Hertz, Ra\'ul Ures

item.title: Pointwise convergence of bilinear ergodic averages for commuting transformations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(X,\mathcal B,\mu)$ be a probability space and let $S,Q:X\to X$ be commuting probability-preserving transformations. Let $1\leq p,q\leq\infty$ satisfy $1/p+1/q\leq1$. We prove that, for every fixed $F\in L^p(\mu)$ and $G\in L^q(\mu)$, the averages $$ \frac1N\sum_{n=1}^N F(S^nx)G(Q^nx) $$ converge almost everywhere as $N\to\infty$. Our proof introduces a new analytic approach that relies on neither the circle method nor characteristic-factor theory. Exploiting the triangular structure arising from commuting transformations, we combine matrix-energy estimates with Gaussian heat-flow arguments to establish pointwise variation inequalities for suitable smooth averages. We then use even and odd Gaussian kernels to recover the convergence of the original averages.
item.dc:creator: Zhuowen Guo, Rongzhong Xiao, Shuhao Zhang

item.title: Uniformly hyperbolic strictly convex billiards
item.description: arXiv:2610.26441v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can a strictly convex billiard be ergodic? For the billiard in a suitable intersection of two circles, we establish \emph{uniform} expansion of vectors in an invariant cone family under the return to a well-chosen section. This is the first and most onerous step towards a forthcoming proof of ergodicity (the Chen--Mohr--Zhang--Zhang conjecture) and statistical properties. Together, this appears to be the first time that a strictly convex billiard is shown to be ergodic.
item.dc:creator: Wentao Fan, Boris Hasselblatt

item.title: Effective intrinsic ergodicity and the transport-entropy inequality: a relation and applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.26588v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Effective intrinsic ergodicity (EIE) quantifies how the pressure defect of an invariant measure controls its distance from an equilibrium state. In this paper, we make explicit the connection between the Einsiedler-Kadyrov-Polo (EKP) inequality, which is central to EIE, and the transport-entropy inequality (TEI). We also extend the finite-state transport-entropy inequality of \cite{CMU19} to topologically mixing countable Markov shifts with the Big Images and Preimages (BIP) property, yielding an EIE estimate in Ornstein's $\bar d$-metric that strengthens \cite{Ruh21}. We also establish a local $\frac{1}{2}$-H\"older bound for the map sending a H\"older potential of finite pressure to its Bowen-Gibbs measure, with respect to the uniform norm on potentials and the $\bar d$-metric on measures. This result extends some aspects of Bhullar's continuity theorem \cite{B25}: it applies to proper subshifts, provides an explicit modulus of continuity with respect to the uniform norm, and does not require strong positive recurrence.
item.dc:creator: Mirmuhsin Maxmud

item.title: Global Dynamics and Periodic-Annulus Bifurcations in a Reversible Quintic Li\'enard System
item.description: arXiv:2610.26699v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the global dynamics and bifurcations of the reversible quintic Li\'enard system $\dot{x}=y$, $\dot{y}=a_0x+a_1x^3+a_2x^5+y(b_0x+b_1x^3)$, with $a_2\ne0$. In the original five-parameter space we treat both signs of $a_2$ and determine all global phase-portrait types on the Poincar\'e disc with one, three, or five finite equilibria. The analysis covers generic and generalized pitchfork, saddle-node, Bogdanov--Takens, and Hopf bifurcations; nilpotent and Hamiltonian degeneracies; bifurcations at infinity; and homoclinic, heteroclinic, limit-cycle-breaking, and periodic-annulus-breaking transitions. For a parameterized class of generalized polynomial Li\'enard systems whose unique finite equilibrium is the nilpotent origin with exactly one elliptic and one hyperbolic sector we establish a unique critical value of the higher-order damping parameter in the intermediate-degree range, nonexistence of a large-scale periodic annulus in the critical-degree case, and its persistence when the restoring degree dominates. Here large-scale means that the annulus closure meets the boundary of the Poincar\'e disc. In the degree range relevant to the quintic system the critical value gives a large-scale periodic-annulus--homoclinic-orbit-family bifurcation marked by a unique separatrix connection to infinity. For the quintic system with multiple finite equilibria periodic-annulus-breaking bifurcations arise from finite separatrix connections or separatrices reaching equilibria at infinity. Using Poincar\'e compactification, local normal forms, rotated vector fields, and separatrix arguments we describe bifurcation sets algebraically or by uniquely characterized critical functions. We obtain complete fixed-coefficient parameter partitions outside $\Omega_{14}$ and determine the admissible critical-surface configurations and their phase portraits inside it.
item.dc:creator: Chen Cao, Nasrin Sadri, Yilei Tang, Zhaoxia Wang

item.title: The moduli space of quasimorphisms on subshifts and its pressure geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.26778v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a metric geometry on the space of positive, linearly growing quasimorphisms on a mixing subshift of finite type. Two such quasimorphisms are identified when their homogenizations agree up to multiplicative scaling. The resulting moduli space carries a natural symmetrised Thurston-type metric, defined from the extremal ratios of their periodic orbit lengths. We prove that this is a genuine metric and determine several global features of the resulting space: it is unbounded, separable, incomplete, and has geodesics that are canonically generated by thermodynamic pressure functions. We then describe the endpoints of these geodesics and develop a boundary theory for our moduli space. We apply this theory to metric structures on right-angled Artin and Coxeter groups. In particular we construct isometric embeddings of geometric moduli spaces into our quasimorphism moduli spaces. As a consequence, Manhattan curves for metrics on these groups are $C^1$, with equality cases characterised by rough similarity of the underlying metrics. This provides insights into Manhattan curves in settings where neither classical thermodynamic formalism for H\"older potentials nor Patterson-Sullivan theory apply. The same construction recovers the corresponding results for hyperbolic groups and places these examples within a common dynamical-geometric framework.
item.dc:creator: Stephen Cantrell, Pablo Carrasco, Emilio Corso, Federico Rodriguez Hertz

item.title: Directional Expansiveness for the chair tiling
item.description: arXiv:2610.26804v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study directional expansiveness of the chair tiling. We show that for every direction $V$ and every $r>0$, there exist distinct chair tilings that agree on $\mathbb{Z}^2\cap V^r$. Hence the chair tiling has no expansive direction.
item.dc:creator: Hyeeun Jang

item.title: An equiregular counterexample to the Sard conjecture for sub-Riemannian endpoint maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.24080v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Lerario, Rizzi and Tiberio disproved the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture with a rank-two distribution on $\mathbb R^4$, of degree of nonholonomy five at the origin, whose endpoint map from that point has no regular values. Their distribution is neither equiregular nor real-analytic, and the equiregular case has remained open. We construct an equiregular rank-two distribution on an open set diffeomorphic to $\mathbb R^9$, with small growth vector $(2,3,5,8,9)$, whose endpoint map from the origin has no regular values. This growth vector is maximal and generic for rank-two distributions in dimension nine, so the failure of the Sard property is not tied to any degeneracy of the growth vector. Singular curves of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio-type structure built from the same coefficient lift, inside the strip where our distribution is defined, to singular curves, and the vertical displacement of a horizontal loop is an explicit strip integral. Realising an open set of vertical displacements by singular loops reduces to a graded moment problem, which we solve with pairs of bumps of opposite winding, an anisotropic rescaling, and an inverse function theorem uniform over infinitely many scales. We also state, with proofs deferred to a planned longer version, two results about our distribution: a description of its abnormal dynamics in the cotangent bundle, which explains the example from a dynamical point of view, and the non-constancy of its Tanaka symbol. The latter motivates an equiregular counterexample in dimension twelve with constant Tanaka symbol (constant nilpotentisation), announced here and to be proved in a separate paper. The longer version will also contain obstructions to real-analytic and lower-dimensional versions, and a transversal variant of the construction, which also leads to a modification of the Lerario--Rizzi--Tiberio counterexample.
item.dc:creator: Bangjie Wang, Igor Zelenko

item.title: Explicit Criteria for Finite-Time Identification in Sparse Primal--Dual Dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2610.24163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study when selected coordinates become and remain zero in a finite-dimensional sparse-regression primal--dual flow and its exact full resolvent iteration. Invariant balls centered at \((0,z)\), with \(z\) strictly dual feasible, give computable deadlines without rank assumptions or optimizer knowledge. The certificates may be available at initialization. We determine the smallest invariant radius for the continuous flow within this family. For a prescribed positive feasibility margin, center selection is convex and admits an exact finite conic formulation. We bound the coordinate margins for all centers in this family and give a normalized correlated example attaining the bound. A composite Bregman Lyapunov estimate proves rank-free convergence without primal uniqueness and finite identification under strict dual margins. Under restricted injectivity, the discrete gap-based deadlines multiplied by the step size tend to the continuous bound for fixed data, observed state, and certificate parameters. Numerical experiments assess certificate timing. A noisy weak-form oscillator regression illustrates the difference between fitted and physical support.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Saoud

item.title: Finiteness of Anosov and pseudo-Anosov flows on hyperbolic 3-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24190v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that for any closed hyperbolic 3-manifold $M$, there are only finitely many Anosov or pseudo-Anosov flows on $M$ up to orbit equivalence.
item.dc:creator: David Gabai, Lily Qiao Li

item.title: Markoff spectra of Hecke groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the initial discrete parts of the Markoff spectra of Hecke groups of index $q\ge 5$. Using a digit expansion associated with geodesics and a Perron-type formula, we classify all bi-infinite digit sequences whose Markoff values lie at or below the first accumulation point. We obtain explicit formulas for the discrete spectral values and identify the sequences realizing them, including those attaining the first accumulation point. We also prove that the infinite family of discrete values increases strictly to this point. Our results recover Vulakh's description of the initial discrete spectra through an explicit symbolic approach.
item.dc:creator: Byungchul Cha, Dong Han Kim

item.title: Pfaffian Positivity for Convex Kernels and Optimal Matching Bounds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24371v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that for all positive, nonincreasing, convex functions $f : (0, \infty) \to (0,\infty)$ and for any collection of $n$ points $x_i \in \mathbb{R}$ with $x_1 < x_2 < \ldots < x_n$ and $n$ even, the Pfaffian of the skew matrix defined by $f(x_j - x_i)$ above the diagonal is positive. More generally, we establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for Pfaffians arising from interval decompositions, which also yields quantitative lower bounds for singly and doubly bordered Pfaffians. Choosing $f(r) = r^{-2}$ proves the three nonvanishing assertions in the conjecture of Albouy and Moeckel. Further, we show that the rainbow bound (the product over the nested matching $\{1,n\}, \{2,n-1\}, \ldots \{n/2, n/2 + 1\}$) is the unique single-matching product that bounds $\mathrm{Pf}(A_f(x))$ below uniformly over $x$ and $f$ positive, nonincreasing, convex.
item.dc:creator: William Johnson

item.title: Adding Heavy-Ball Momentum to Distributed Constrained Optimization for Energy Resource Management Subject to Time-Delays and Quantization
item.description: arXiv:2610.24421v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper studies a hybrid discrete-time signed gradient-consensus method with heavy-ball momentum, paired communication delays, and fixed logarithmic quantization. The method preserves the aggregate supply-demand equality at every iteration. For a static connected undirected graph and bounded delays, a Lyapunov-Krasovskii analysis establishes practical stability by isolating the discontinuous quantization error as an additive disturbance and closing a computable invariant-sublevel argument. The resulting ergodic residual bound is quadratic in the quantization resolution, and exact convergence to the smooth penalized equality-constrained optimizer is recovered in the unquantized case. For delay-free unquantized quadratic costs, an exact modal analysis identifies the heavy-ball stability region and optimal parameters, with the predicted rate validated on a fixed sparse network. A reproducible delayed experiment reports all constants and a certificate whose guaranteed steady-state level lies below the reported initialization. A separate mixed generator-battery experiment exercises the signed update directly. Finite smooth penalties approximate, but do not generally enforce, the local box constraints exactly.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadreza Doostmohammadian, Sergio Pequito

item.title: Lyapunov-Krasovsky Functionals and the Existence of Unbounded Solutions of Functional-Differential Equations of Retarded Type
item.description: arXiv:2610.24620v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, the concepts of unboundedness and partial unboundedness of solutions of functional-differential equations of retarded type are introduced. On the basis of the method of Lyapunov-Krasovsky functionals, sufficient conditions for the existence of partially unbounded solutions are obtained. As corollaries, sufficient conditions for the existence of unbounded solutions are obtained.
item.dc:creator: Lapin K. S., Lapin S. V

item.title: Three Machines Suffice for Local Hardening of Electromechanical Oscillations
item.description: arXiv:2610.24760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The single-degree-of-freedom swing equation with sinusoidal coupling is locally softening: its oscillation frequency decreases with oscillation level near a stable equilibrium. Nonlinear modal interaction, however, can reverse this trend in multimachine systems. This letter gives a necessary-and-sufficient condition for strict leading-order local hardening, measured with respect to canonical action, in two symmetric three-machine operating-point families with equal or opposite power injections at the equal-inertia machines. An exact two-coordinate reduction expresses the condition in terms of a squared modal-frequency ratio and a dimensionless nonlinear coupling measure. The proof retains the induced mean shift and second harmonic and shows that the companion modal family remains locally softening. The criterion recovers both an equal-inertia hardening example and an exact large-inertia threshold. Coherent aggregation recovers the two-machine softening law, whereas the infinite-bus limit retains two dynamic rotor angles and permits hardening. An exact coherent-group extension preserves the selected periodic family, frequency, and canonical action for every finite machine count greater than two. Thus, three finite-inertia machines are the minimum permitting local hardening in the stated undamped, lossless classical model.
item.dc:creator: Kai Sun

item.title: Hodge-Carleman estimates and global attractors for heterogeneous elastic waves with localized damping on Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.24924v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the long-time dynamics of the semilinear Lam\'e system of isotropic elasticity on a compact Riemannian manifold with boundary, for a heterogeneous medium whose density and Lam\'e moduli vary in space, under a frictional dissipation which acts only on an open set $\omega$. The elastic operator is the divergence of the Hooke stress tensor, and the starting point is a structural identity which shows that the dilatation and the vorticity of the displacement satisfy wave equations with the pressure and the shear speeds, respectively, coupled to the displacement only through first-order terms. A single weight function, free of critical points and strictly convex with respect to the two ray metrics of the medium, then serves for the displacement, its dilatation and its vorticity alike, and this Hodge structure yields Carleman estimates for the Lam\'e operator with variable coefficients at two energy levels, provided that $\omega$ contains a neighbourhood of the boundary and that such a weight exists on the undamped region. The hypothesis is fulfilled on every compact manifold with boundary by damping regions of arbitrarily small volume. From these estimates we derive unique continuation for elastic waves with bounded, merely measurable, time-dependent potentials and an internal observability inequality, which in turn yield, for subcritical restoring forces in dimension three, a compact global attractor which coincides with the unstable manifold of the equilibria, has finite fractal dimension and is bounded in $(H^2\cap H^1_0)\times H^1_0$, together with a generalized exponential attractor.
item.dc:creator: Paulo N. Seminario-Huertas

item.title: Increased-Order Generalized Synchronization in Memristive Neurons: Analytical and Data-Driven Approaches
item.description: arXiv:2610.25164v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate increased-order generalized synchronization between four- and five-dimensional memristive Hindmarsh--Rose neurons, focusing on the selection and stabilization of the synchronization map. An analytical construction combines a prescribed nonlinear map with adaptive control, retaining the memristive switching contribution explicitly in the error dynamics. Lyapunov analysis establishes asymptotic synchronization under uniform strict dissipativity and yields a switching-independent decrease estimate outside an explicit error neighborhood. Numerical simulations exhibit error decay beyond the sufficient convergence conditions. A complementary data-driven construction uses next-generation reservoir computing to learn predictors from uncoupled full-state trajectories and an affine synchronization map through dynamical consistency. The resulting sampled-data controller achieves small residual tracking errors without access to the governing equations. Relative to a reference map within the data-driven framework, the learned map reduces median control effort approximately eightfold while improving tracking accuracy. These results connect synchronization-map selection with conditional convergence guarantees and reduced control requirements.
item.dc:creator: Dennis Mustafi\'{c}, Marius E. Yamakou

item.title: Free abelian group actions on projective fibered varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.25778v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $X$ be an $n$-dimensional normal projective variety of Kodaira dimension $\kappa$ and $G$ an abelian subgroup of automorphisms such that all elements of $G\backslash \{\mathrm{id}\}$ are of positive entropy. Dinh and Sibony showed that $G$ is actually free abelian of rank $\le n-\kappa-1$. In this paper, we show that after replacing $G$ by a finite-index subgroup, there exists a G-Equivariant Minimal Model Program for the pair $(X, G)$ when $\mathrm{rank}(G)=n-\kappa-1$ and $\kappa>0$, and the very general fiber of the final model is a klt Calabi-Yau surface or a $Q$-abelian variety provided that the termination of flips holds in this setting.
item.dc:creator: Sichen Li

item.title: The global structure of bi-rotational self-shrinkers
item.description: arXiv:2610.25831v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We describe the global structure of the self-shrinkers of the mean curvature flow in $\mathbb{R}^{p+q+2}$ invariant under $O(p+1)\times O(q+1)$, without assuming properness or embeddedness. The main tool is a pair of piecewise monotone quantities along the profile curves, in the spirit of Hsiang's analysis of constant mean curvature hypersurfaces. We prove that every such self-shrinker other than the two invariant cylinders intersects both of them transversely, and all of them except the Clifford minimal cone are complete. Apart from those of the cylinders, each end is either asymptotic to a cone or meets both cylinders infinitely many times. Consequently, a complete noncompact example is proper if and only if all its ends are asymptotically conical, and this is equivalent to polynomial volume growth, to finite entropy, and to finitely many intersections with the cylinders. The reduced flow preserves a finite measure, and for almost every initial condition the profile curve is either closed or generates a complete nonproper self-shrinker of infinite entropy. We also bound the winding of the profile curve by its number of cylinder crossings and localize its self-intersections.
item.dc:creator: Greg\'orio Silva Neto

item.title: On the group of automorphisms of the escaping sets of H\'{e}non maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.25891v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this article, we provide an explicit description of $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$, the group of automorphisms of the escaping set $I_H^+$ of a H\'enon map that induce the identity on its fundamental group. More precisely, for a H\'enon map $H(x,y)=(y,p(y)-\delta x),$ where $p$ is a polynomial of degree $d\geq 2$ and $\delta\neq 0$, we show that $\operatorname{Aut}_1(I_H^+)$ is completely determined by the degree and the coefficients of $p$. Thus, the automorphism group of the escaping set, subject to the prescribed topological constraint, can be explicitly characterized in terms of the underlying H\'enon map.
item.dc:creator: Mahima, Ratna Pal

item.title: Lagrangian invariant tori for completely resonant nonlinear Schr{\"o}dinger equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.26044v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study small solutions of the parameterless nonlinear Schr{\"o}dinger equations on the circle. In this regime, the nonlinearity is perturbative and the system is thus nearly integrable. We prove the persistence, in the presence of nonlinearity, of full-dimensional tori. We justify this denomination by proving that they are Lagrangian in the sense that, although they are not submanifolds (since they are compact), at every point their tangent cone is a Lagrangian subspace. This is the first result of this type for an equation without an infinity of external random parameters. We achieve this by establishing new fine decay and uniformity properties of the amplitude-to-frequency map. This is the main technical novelty of this paper. It allows us to modulate all the frequencies and thus obtain non-resonance conditions without any assumption on the choice of the tangential sites.
item.dc:creator: Joackim Bernier (LMJL), Michela Procesi

item.title: On the Peak Estimation of Scalar Polynomial Systems via Integrability
item.description: arXiv:2610.26132v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a convergent occupation measure framework for peak estimation of scalar polynomial dynamical systems with no a priori state bound. The key observation is that scalar trajectories satisfy a uniform weighted integrability bound whose exponent precisely compensates for the singularity introduced by polynomial compactification. This yields a finite measure formulation with polynomial data. We establish a superposition principle for the resulting weighted continuity equation, prove no relaxation gap and establish convergence of the associated moment-sum-of-squares hierarchy.
item.dc:creator: Karol\'ina Sehnalov\'a

item.title: Fate of Arnold tongues and canards in Mobius systems with noise
item.description: arXiv:2610.26354v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We consider a class of noisy dynamical systems on the two-dimensional torus whose phase evolution is governed by Mobius transformations. In the deterministic limit, these systems favor phase-locking that is described by the band-gap structure of an associated Schrodinger equation with a periodic potential. We use the Wentzel-Kramers-Brillouin method to characterize this structure in the slow-fast limit. Then we show that large-deviation theory describes fluctuations of the finite-time rotation number, whereas weak-noise escape actions determine the exponential scale of rare phase slips. These estimates provide quantitative criteria for metastable phase-locking and melting of Arnold tongues over a prescribed observation time. We derive sufficient conditions for stochastic trajectories to follow prescribed canard segments. With controlled entrance errors, exponential amplification of fluctuations along repelling branches leads to an exponentially small sufficient noise scale for canard persistence in the slow-forcing limit.
item.dc:creator: Artem Alexandrov

item.title: Simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation for stochastic reaction networks
item.description: arXiv:2610.26361v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Uncovering stochastic reaction networks from data is central to single-cell biology. Simulation-based inference has evolved into a flexible paradigm for this purpose, circumventing the computational intractability of the likelihood. Notably, approximate Bayesian computation performs this inference by carrying out extensive Gillespie simulations, usually at a high computational cost. Here, we propose a simulation-free approximate Bayesian computation (SFABC) framework that avoids both simulation and explicit likelihood solutions of the network dynamics. Instead, SFABC exploits the Chemical Master Equation to formulate a tractable convex optimization with ensuing constraints, which are then used to accept sampled parameters consistent with the observed data. The resulting posterior approximation comes with theoretical guarantees: it can be tightened systematically, and it provably converges to the exact Bayesian posterior distributions. Using synthetic benchmarks, we show that SFABC matches the accuracy of standard simulation-based algorithms at a substantially reduced computational cost. We then showcase the applicability of SFABC to experimental systems biology by analyzing gene transcription bursting kinetics from snapshot, time-resolved, and cell-cycle-resolved single-cell data.
item.dc:creator: Zekai Li, Mauricio Barahona, Philipp Thomas

item.title: Semiclassical measures for quantized elliptic and parabolic symplectic linear maps of the multidimensional torus
item.description: arXiv:2610.26382v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the semiclassical measures associated to the quantum map on the torus obtained by quantizing integer symplectic linear maps, focusing on periodic matrices and certain parabolic matrices. More precisely, we consider the time-one map of the completely integrable flows generated by Hamiltonians of the form H(x, $\xi$) = Q($\xi$)/2 where Q is an integral quadratic form. We prove that the set of semiclassical measures associated to a periodic matrix A coincides with the set of invariant probability measures of A. The semiclassical measures of parabolic matrices on T${}^2$ are explicitly characterized by proving that they have at most three nonzero Fourier coefficients in position. A partial quantum ergodicity statement for parabolic matrices is obtained by proving a sharp bound on the quantum variance and some examples are built in higher dimensions. In particular, starting from T___ there always exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position has only nonzero Fourier coefficients. Moreover, if Q is isotropic over the rationals, then there exist semiclassical measures whose projection on the position concentrate on some subtori. A link is made with the semiclassical measures of the Laplacian on the torus.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Ferrari-Dominguez (IRMA)

item.title: Data Center Oscillation Isolation and Grid Support: Fundamental Limits and Source-Selective Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.26812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The grid integration of large data centers poses a growing power-system stability challenge. Rapidly varying computing demand can induce oscillations, while the facilities must provide a prescribed response to grid disturbances. Existing controls address load fluctuations and grid support but do not establish their jointly achievable performance. This paper derives fundamental limits and develops a source-selective controller for simultaneous oscillation isolation and grid support. A coupled closed-loop model gives a condition for distinguishing disturbance sources and reveals a direct isolation-support conflict under grid-import-power feedback alone; additional electrical measurements can remove this pointwise conflict but leave a conditional cross-frequency sensitivity limit. Guided by these limits, we design a local residual-feedback storage controller through convex frequency-domain optimization with stability, isolation, and grid-response constraints across operating points. Tests on a single-generator interconnection and a modified nine-bus network show stronger oscillation isolation than equal-order optimized comparators while meeting the prescribed grid response across operating points.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Feng

item.title: Complexity of measure-induced maps
item.description: arXiv:2503.22944v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A classical result by Glasner and Weiss states that a map $f$ has zero topological entropy if and only if its measure-induced map $f_*$, defined as the push-forward of a measure, does. In this work, we use generalized entropy to distinguish the complexity of these maps and prove that the measure-induced map is strictly more complex whenever the generalized entropy of the original map is nonzero and is not an abstract order of growth. Moreover, we show that the complexity of the measure-induced map is of at most polynomial type when the nonwandering set of $f$ is finite. For homeomorphisms of infinite spaces, this bound is attained, so measure-induced maps of Morse--Smale diffeomorphisms cannot be distinguished from one another.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Lacerda

item.title: An Algebraic Approach to Periodicity and Complexity of Delone Sets
item.description: arXiv:2504.20709v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the connection between local complexity and periodicity of Delone sets using an algebraic approach based on annihilators, that is, finite linear relations between translations of a configuration. We model colored Delone sets (Delone multisets) as $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations, that is, functions on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with finite range, and extend the notions of annihilators and periodizers from $\mathbb{Z}^d$-configurations to the geometric setting of Delone sets. Our main results describe the structure imposed by the existence of non-trivial annihilators. We show that any $\mathbb{R}^d$-configuration admitting non-trivial annihilators has an annihilator of a particularly simple form, namely a product of finitely many difference operators corresponding to translations in pairwise rationally independent directions. We further improve this result and prove that for configurations supported on Delone sets of finite local complexity (FLC), the corresponding directions can be chosen pairwise linearly independent over $\mathbb{R}$. As a consequence of the existence of the special annihilator, we show that $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations with annihilators admit a decomposition into finitely many components that are periodic in pairwise rationally independent directions. Moreover, we connect local complexity with algebraic structure by proving that Meyer sets with sufficiently slow patch complexity growth have low pattern complexity and hence admit non-trivial annihilators. Finally, we establish a sufficient and necessary condition under which the existence of suitable annihilators forces periodicity of $\mathbb{R}^d$-configurations supported on FLC Delone sets.
item.dc:creator: Pyry Herva, Jarkko Kari

item.title: Unstable entropy for Anosov diffeomorphisms on the 3-torus
item.description: arXiv:2509.09520v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For Anosov diffeomorphisms on the $3$-torus which are strongly partially hyperbolic with expanding center, we construct systems of strong unstable and center stable Margulis measures which are holonomy-invariant. This allows us to obtain a characterization of the measures of maximal unstable entropy in terms of their conditional measures along the strong unstable leaves. Moreover, we show that the Margulis systems identify with Pollicott-Ruelle (co)-resonant states for the action on 2-forms. This shows that the unstable topological entropy and a measure of maximal unstable entropy can be retrieved from the spectral approach.
item.dc:creator: Tristan Humbert

item.title: Thermodynamic formalism and multifractal analysis of Birkhoff averages for non-uniformly expanding R\'{e}nyi interval maps with countably many branches
item.description: arXiv:2511.02266v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study the multifractal spectrum of Birkhoff averages for non-uniformly expanding R\'{e}nyi interval maps with countably many branches. Our main theorem substantially strengthens conditional variational formulas established by Jaerisch and Takahasi. Furthermore, our results enable a detailed analysis of Khinchin exponents and arithmetic means of backward continued fraction expansions in terms of the Hausdorff dimension. We also give a positive answer to the conjecture of Jaerisch and Takahasi. In addition, we develop the thermodynamic formalism for non-uniformly expanding R\'{e}nyi interval maps with countably many branches.
item.dc:creator: Yuya Arima

item.title: On the intersection of Cantor sets and products of random matrices
item.description: arXiv:2512.02675v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Author's follow-up comment: The line of research pursued in this paper has been developed substantially further in my subsequent paper, Lyapunov exponents for random products of non-negative matrices (arXiv:2602.23317). I will therefore not pursue separate journal publication of the present paper. Original abstract: Kenyon and Peres (1991) showed that the Hausdorff dimension of intersections of randomly translated Cantor sets can be expressed in terms of the top Lyapunov exponent of a product of random matrices, and this exponent can be written as an integral with respect to stationary measures on the projective line. Although explicit computations are available when stationary measures are discrete, the continuous case has remained challenging. In this paper we introduce new combinatorial and analytic tools that allow us to compute the Lyapunov exponent, and hence the Hausdorff dimension, in a broad class of examples where stationary measures are continuous. As an application, we complete the dimension computation in the setting where a single digit is forbidden; for example, we determine the Hausdorff dimension of the intersection of the middle-seventh Cantor set with a random translate of itself.
item.dc:creator: Nima Alibabaei

item.title: Set-Valued Riemann-Liouville integral and some Regular Selections
item.description: arXiv:2512.23584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we introduce the notion of the Riemann-Liouville fractional integral of set-valued mappings via integrable selections. We establish fundamental properties of this fractional integral, including convexity, boundedness, and continuity with respect to the Hausdorff metric. The investigation of preservation of regularity under fractional integration with respect to the Hausdorff metric is given. We show that bounded variation and Lipschitz continuity of a set-valued mapping are inherited by its Riemann-Liouville fractional integral. We discuss the existence of regular selections for the fractional integral under the corresponding regularity assumptions on the original mapping. In the scalar case, we further identify extremal selections given by the pointwise minimum and maximum of the fractional integral and show that they possess the same regularity properties. Finally, we discuss possible applications in differential inclusion and directions for future research.
item.dc:creator: Subhash Chandra, Syed Abbas

item.title: Rate-induced tipping in a solvable model with the Allee effect
item.description: arXiv:2601.20128v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present a novel exactly solvable ordinary differential equation model for rate-induced tipping: a dynamic phenomenon of dynamical systems where a time-dependent parameter triggers the transition of stability of a system. Our model contains an Allee effect that induces a saddle point and admits an explicit solution along with the extinction threshold of a time-dependent Allee parameter. More specifically, we derive an integral inequality that serves as a necessary condition for the occurrence of rate-induced tipping. A remarkable point in the proposed model is that it can handle population extinction such that the solution completely vanishes in a finite amount of time. An unconditionally stable cubature method suitable for our model is proposed, and its superiority over the classical forward Euler method is discussed. As a proof of concept, the model reproduces the rise and fall of the membership of inland fisheries cooperatives in Japan from 1963 to 2023. The proposed model serves as a tractable tool for studying R-tipping phenomena.
item.dc:creator: Hidekazu Yoshioka

item.title: Semialgebraic interior layers in root closures of bounded-height integer polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2603.07397v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Finite-degree root plots of bounded-height monic integer polynomials can exhibit gaps around interior points of their root closures. Outside the closed unit disk, these closures coincide with Mandelbrot sets for affine iterated function systems with collinear digits. We construct explicit semialgebraic interior layers, certified when finite inverse orbits enter canonical self-covering parallelograms. Such parallelograms exist exactly in the non-real lens, which contains the non-real locus precisely from twenty maps onward. Within the non-real lens, limits of each capture level are captured within two additional steps, optimally, and the layers recover the locus by closure. The layers expose persistent interior deficits: explicit quadratic parameters evade every finite level; sufficiently close distinct parameters have logarithmically growing capture depths; the underlying lattice obstruction yields degree-dependent root-free radii, explaining such gaps. For non-real parameters of modulus at least the square root of the number of maps, exact enclosure trees have sharp, alphabet-independent branching bounds.
item.dc:creator: Bernat Espigule, David Juher

item.title: Extreme value theorem for geodesic flow on the quotient of the theta group
item.description: arXiv:2603.07649v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an extreme value theorem for the geodesic flow $g_t$ on the hyperbolic surface $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$ associated with the theta group $\Theta$. To capture excursions into both cusps of this surface, we introduce a generalized continued fraction algorithm obtained by splicing the even and odd--odd continued fraction maps into a single dynamical system. We prove that the natural extension of this map is isomorphic to the first return map of the geodesic flow on a suitable cross-section. Using spectral properties of the associated transfer operator, we derive a Galambos-type extreme value law for the digits of the spliced continued fraction. This symbolic result is then translated into a geometric extreme value theorem describing maximal cusp excursions of geodesics on $\Theta\backslash\mathbb{H}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Jaelin Kim, Seul Bee Lee, Seonhee Lim

item.title: When is cumulative dose response monotonic? Analysis of incoherent feedforward motifs
item.description: arXiv:2604.01573v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the monotonicity of the cumulative dose response (cDR) for a class of incoherent feedforward motifs (IFFM) systems with linear intermediate dynamics and nonlinear output dynamics. While the instantaneous dose response (DR) may be nonmonotone with respect to the input, the cDR can still be monotone. To analyze this phenomenon, we derive an integral representation of the sensitivity of cDR with respect to the input and establish general sufficient conditions for both monotonicity and nonmonotonicity. These results reduce the problem to verifying qualitative sign properties along system trajectories. The structural conditions identify eight canonical IFFM models, four of which are analyzed in detail within the proposed framework. In particular, IFFM1 and IFFM3 exhibit monotone cDR despite potentially nonmonotone DR, while IFFM2 is monotone already at the level of DR, which implies monotonicity of cDR. In contrast, IFFM4 exhibits nonmonotone cDR. Numerical simulations indicate that these properties persist beyond the structured initial conditions used in the analysis. Overall, our results provide a unified framework for understanding how system structure shapes monotonicity in cumulative input--output responses.
item.dc:creator: Moh Kamalul Wafi, Arthur C. B. de Oliveira, Eduardo D. Sontag

item.title: Non-Autonomous Return Dynamics for Nested Convex Bodies:\\ Cubic Tangency, Summable Geometric Variation, and Critical Regimes
item.description: arXiv:2604.09872v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study a non-autonomous geometric dynamics generated by successive normal transitions between nested convex boundaries sharing a common tangency point. For \(C_{k+1}\subset C_k\subset\mathbb{R}^2\), let \(\mathcal G_k:\partial C_k\to\partial C_{k+1}\) be the first intersection of the inward normal ray with the next boundary. In signed arclength coordinates, the induced scalar map \(G_k\) is tangent to the identity to second order. Writing the boundaries locally as graphs \(f_k\), we prove the uniform defect estimate \[ |G_k(s)-s|\leq C\|f_{k+1}-f_k\|_{C^2}|s|^3. \] The first nonlinear term is cubic: \[ G_k(s)=s+\beta_k s^3+O(s^4), \qquad \beta_k= \frac{(\kappa_{k+1}-\kappa_k)(\kappa_{k+1}-2\kappa_k)}{6}, \] where \(\kappa_k=-f_k''(0)\). Higher coefficients satisfy a diagonal-vanishing principle: they vanish when the corresponding boundary jets coincide. If the geometric variation is summable, \(\sum_{k\geq0}\|f_{k+1}-f_k\|_{C^2}<\infty\), then the full transition defect is summable. Every sufficiently small nonzero orbit has finite total drift and converges to a nonzero limit; hence the common tangency point is Lyapunov stable but not locally attractive. The non-autonomous composition defines a limiting displacement map tangent to the identity. We also study abstract parabolic recurrences with nonsummable nonlinear drift. A weighted comparison principle yields polynomial and logarithmic asymptotic laws, including critical quartic and quintic regimes: \[ s_k\sim(3c\log k)^{-1/3}, \qquad s_k\sim(4c\log k)^{-1/4}. \] These abstract regimes are kept separate from the geometric theory. The main open problem is to determine which critical parabolic behaviors can actually be realized by nested convex boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed El Morsalani, Mohammed Barkatou

item.title: Lyapunov exponents for uniformly hyperbolic random matrix products
item.description: arXiv:2604.12244v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider a finite family of invertible $2 \times 2$ real matrices and a transitive Markov shift on the index set. Let $\lambda$ be the top Lyapunov exponent for random matrix products driven by the Markov shift. We prove that, if the matrices are projectively uniformly hyperbolic with respect to the Markov shift, then $\lambda$ admits an explicit representation in terms of an infinite matrix. This rapidly convergent representation yields a polynomial-time algorithm for approximating $\lambda$: only $O\big( (\log(1/\varepsilon))^3 \big)$ arithmetic operations are needed to achieve error $\varepsilon$. Furthermore, $\lambda$ depends real analytically on the matrix entries and the transition probabilities near a projectively uniformly hyperbolic system, and each Taylor coefficient can be approximated in polynomial time.
item.dc:creator: Nima Alibabaei

item.title: A nonlinear version of the $\alpha$-Kakutani equidistribution problem
item.description: arXiv:2605.16156v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we extend results of Kakutani; Adler and Flatto; Smilansky; Pollicott and Sewell on the equidistribution of endpoints generated by interval-splitting procedures. We study a nonlinear version of the problem generated by a finite or countable family of $\mathcal{C}^{1+ \varepsilon}$ contractions and prove Lebesgue equidistribution under suitable nonlattice and thermodynamic regularity assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Ignacio Rojas

item.title: Geometric Methods for Stochastic Dynamical Systems: A Concise Introduction
item.description: arXiv:2607.27237v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Geometric methods are indispensable for analyzing, predicting, and mitigating the complex behaviors inherent in nonlinear systems. In this regime, the most probable transition path minimizes the Onsager-Machlup action functional, marking the likeliest route across an energy barrier. Lifting the analysis from individual sample paths to the infinite-dimensional space of probability densities, the book recasts these transitions as Schr\"odinger bridges - optimal paths between boundary distributions defined by minimizing relative entropy - and shows that the Onsager-Machlup path emerges as a special case when metastable states are idealized as Dirac masses. Generalizing further through {\alpha}-divergences, which connect to entropies and the thermodynamic cost of nonequilibrium transitions, it introduces information geodesics as the resulting optimal density paths, offering a unified geometric account of how complex systems move between metastable regimes under uncertainty.
item.dc:creator: Jinqiao Duan, Ting Gao, Qiao Huang, Yuanfei Huang

item.title: Explicit exposure of Haar measure
item.description: arXiv:2608.21299v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We solve the problem, posed some twenty years ago, of explicitly constructing a continuous function whose unique maximizing measure for the doubling map is Lebesgue measure. This is a special case of a more general result: given a nontrivial compact metrizable abelian group and a continuous endomorphism for which normalised Haar measure is ergodic, we explicitly construct a continuous function on the group for which Haar measure is the unique invariant maximizing measure. The function is the uniform limit of a recursively defined sequence of trigonometric polynomials with rational coefficients; every parameter of the recursion is given by an explicit formula, every step is exact, and the rate of convergence is explicit. For expanding circle endomorphisms, ergodic toral endomorphisms, and the one-sided full shift, the construction can moreover be arranged so that the function is given by a Fourier series that converges uniformly in the classical frequency order, each of whose coefficients is rational and computable exactly by a finite procedure. We also show that no continuous function whose unique maximizing measure is Haar measure has absolutely summable Fourier coefficients, so that no such function lies in the Wiener algebra. For expanding maps of the circle, the Fourier coefficients of a continuous function with a unique maximizing measure of full support admit no closed form, in the sense that they satisfy no linear recurrence with polynomial coefficients; this follows from a result of independent interest, that a continuous function on the circle whose Fourier coefficients satisfy such a recurrence is H\"older continuous.
item.dc:creator: Yixuan Huang, Oliver Jenkinson, Zhiqiang Li, Hang Zhao

item.title: Unique ergodicity, and not, for primitive substitutions on compact alphabets containing isolated points
