item.description: arXiv:2609.07550v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider generalised subshifts generated by continuous substitution on compact Hausdorff alphabets. Although primitivity still implies minimality of the subshift generated by the substitution, Durand, Ormes and Petite showed, in contrast to the finite case, that primitivity no longer implies unique ergodicity, by constructing counterexamples with Cantor alphabet. Here we show that, even for the arguably simplest case of the one-point compactification of the natural numbers, primitivity is still insufficient for unique ergodicity, or even the existence of a natural length function (NLF). In previous work with Ma\~{n}ibo and Rust we showed that, for irreducible substitutions, unique ergodicity and existence of a NLF follow from strong power convergence of the renormalised substitution operator \(T\); criteria were also developed that can sometimes confirm strong power convergence. Here we show the converse, so that strong power convergence of \(T\) is equivalent to having both unique ergodicity and a NLF. We then consider the case of alphabets with only finitely many accumulation points, showing how upper bounds (and usually an exact formula) for the essential spectral radius of \(T\) can be derived from associated finite substitutions, determined by the behaviour of substitution of the accumulation points. For many primitive substitutions this can be used to prove quasi-compactness of \(T\), and thus unique ergodicity. For primitive substitutions on alphabets with at least one isolated point, we show that strong power convergence and quasi-compactness of \(T\) are equivalent and, in fact, that these properties are equivalent to iteration of substitution growing words in length uniformly across all seeds in the alphabet.
item.dc:creator: James J. Walton

item.title: Twisted Patterson-Sullivan densities on nilpotent covers for Anosov subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2609.27125v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Gamma<\mathsf{SL}(d,\mathbb R)$ be a torsion-free, Zariski-dense Borel-Anosov subgroup, and let $\varphi$ be a linear functional positive on the limit cone of $\Gamma$. For every $\chi \in \operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma, \mathbb R)$, we construct twisted $(\varphi,\chi)$-conformal densities and prove their existence, uniqueness and ergodicity. For every non-trivial normal subgroup $\Gamma_0\lhd\Gamma$ with nilpotent quotient, we classify the ergodic $\varphi$-conformal densities of $\Gamma_0$ in terms of characters of $\Gamma/\Gamma_0$. Up to scaling, they are naturally parametrized by $\operatorname{Hom}(\Gamma/\Gamma_0,\mathbb R)$, and their dimensions are precisely the critical exponents of the corresponding twisted Poincar\'e series. We also prove a shadow lemma for twisted densities of normal subgroups, with estimates uniform over densities with fixed parameters, and a twisted Hopf-Tsuji-Sullivan theorem.
item.dc:creator: Krishnendu Gongopadhyay, Neelanjan Mondal

item.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.14282v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show that the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard disks moving freely on the plane is at least exponential in $n$.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: Finiteness of planar central configurations of five bodies for all positive masses: On Smale's sixth problem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16107v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that for every choice of five positive masses the planar five-body problem has only finitely many central configurations up to rotation, translation and scaling. This answers Smale's sixth problem for five bodies. Albouy and Kaloshin proved the statement for all masses outside a closed algebraic subset of codimension two of the mass space. We keep their classification of singular sequences and combine local boundary analysis with a global argument on an algebraic curve. We exclude Diagrams~1, 2, 4, 6 and~8 for complex germs, Diagram~7 on curves through real configurations, and Diagram~3 on curves with a positive arc. For Diagrams~5 and~9, direct order estimates show that the product $\Delta$ of all squared mutual distances tends to zero. On a hypothetical curve containing a positive arc, a first pole of a four-product therefore gives a zero of $\Delta$. On the completed curve, $\Delta$ must then have a pole elsewhere. The identity $\Delta^4=\prod_{i<j}p_{ij}$ forces a four-product to have a pole there, contradicting the same vanishing conclusion. The computer-assisted inputs concern Diagrams~2, 3 and~6 and use exact algebra, interval arithmetic and ball arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Zhe Chen, Zhicheng Tong

item.title: Reeb orbits frequently intersecting a symplectic surface
item.description: arXiv:2504.19332v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Consider a symplectic surface in a three-dimensional contact manifold with boundary on Reeb orbits (periodic orbits of the Reeb vector field). We assume that the rotation numbers of the boundary Reeb orbits satisfy a certain inequality, and we also make a technical assumption that the Reeb vector field has a particular ``nice'' form near the boundary of the surface. We then show that there exist Reeb orbits which intersect the interior of the surface, with a lower bound on the frequency of these intersections in terms of the symplectic area of the surface and the contact volume of the three-manifold. No genericity of the contact form is assumed. As a corollary of the main result, we obtain a generalization of various recent results relating the mean action of periodic orbits to the Calabi invariant for area-preserving surface diffeomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Michael Hutchings

item.title: The Restricted Three-Body Problem as a Perturbed Duffing Equation
item.description: arXiv:2505.07104v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the restricted circular planar three-body problem. We prove that for every negative Jacobi constant of sufficiently large magnitude, the surface of unperturbed parabolic solutions breaks to induce homoclinic tangles for all but at most finitely many mass ratios of primaries. Our approach relies on reformulating the restricted three-body problem as a perturbed Duffing equation by introducing new coordinate transformations. This enables us to capture the order of the singularities involved through a renormalized Duffing Hamiltonian structure, to derive the existence and analytic dependence of the invariant manifolds on the mass ratio of the primaries, and to evaluate the Poincar\'e-Melnikov integral directly through the explicit homoclinic solution of the unperturbed Duffing equation. Compared to existing works, our proof is significantly simpler and more direct. Moreover, the paper is self-contained: we do not rely on McGehee's analysis in \cite{Mc} to justify the applicability of the Poincar\'e-Melnikov method.
item.dc:creator: Rongchang Liu, Qiudong Wang

item.title: Topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems
item.description: arXiv:2509.13537v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the topological entropy of nonlinear time-varying systems. We establish conditions under which entropy is independent of the initial time and derive two general upper bounds based on the matrix measure of the system Jacobian and the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, respectively. A general lower bound is also obtained using the trace of the Jacobian. For interconnected systems, we first derive an upper bound using the matrix measure of an interconnection matrix constructed from the Jacobian blocks. We then establish a new upper bound based on the spectral abscissa of a Metzler comparison matrix, incorporating the interconnection structure through subsystem-wise trajectory-separation analysis. This bound also recovers the two general upper bounds as special cases. All bounds depend on asymptotic properties of the Jacobian over reachable sets or their convex hulls. Simple examples show that either general upper bound may be tighter, while a time-varying Lorenz system illustrates the effects of norm selection and subsystem decomposition.
item.dc:creator: Guosong Yang, Daniel Liberzon

item.title: Geodesics in the Deep Linear Network
item.description: arXiv:2510.07324v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We derive a general system of ordinary differential equations and associated explicit solutions in a special case for geodesics between full rank matrices in the deep linear network geometry. In the process, we find horizontal straight lines in the invariant balanced manifold that remain geodesics under Riemannian submersion.
item.dc:creator: Alan Chen

item.title: Twisted operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary graphs
item.description: arXiv:2511.07906v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study self-similar groupoid actions on arbitrary directed graphs together with $\mathbb{T}$-valued twists that exhaust the second cohomology group of the associated Zappa-Sz\'ep product category. We define and analyse the associated universal, reduced, and essential $C^*$-algebras, along with their Toeplitz versions and core subalgebras. In fact, we develop our theory in the more general setting of $L^P$-operator algebras, where $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$ is any non-empty set of parameters. This includes $C^*$-algebras, $L^p$-operator algebras and symmetrised $L^{p,*}$-operator algebras for $p\in [1,\infty]$, as special cases. We use three complementary approaches: twisted inverse semigroups, twisted ample groupoids, and $C^*$-correspondences. We provide, in terms of the self-similar action, general characterisations of topological freeness, minimality, Hausdorffness, finite non-Hausdorffness, effectiveness, and local contractiveness for the associated ample groupoids. We generalise the classical Cuntz--Krieger Uniqueness and Coburn--Toeplitz Uniqueness Theorems for graph $C^*$-algebras to twisted $L^P$-operator algebras of self-similar groupoid actions. We characterise when the natural inclusions are Cartan, give checkable criteria for simplicity and pure infiniteness of the essential algebras, and discuss when the universal and reduced algebras coincide. We also provide conditions that ensure the singular ideals vanish. Using the groupoid model we show that for any $P\subseteq [1,\infty]$, the $L^P$-operator algebra of a contracting self-similar action is simple if and only if the corresponding Steinberg algebra is simple. Using the Toeplitz-Pimsner model, we prove that for the universal groupoid of any self-similar groupoid action on a row-finite graph, the singular $C^*$-algebraic ideal always vanishes.
item.dc:creator: B. K. Kwa\'sniewski, A. Mundey

item.title: Trajectory arclength reveals chaos
item.description: arXiv:2602.07660v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the time-averaged phase space arclength of a trajectory, expressed through a normalized Lagrangian descriptor, as a trajectory-based diagnostic for distinguishing regular and chaotic dynamics. The proposed indicator, $\Omega$, is computed by integrating the equations of motion together with a single scalar arclength-accumulation equation and therefore does not require variational equations, neighboring trajectories, or spatial derivatives of a Lagrangian descriptor field. Using Birkhoff's ergodic theorem together with estimates for quasiperiodic motion and correlation-based arguments for chaotic ergodic dynamics, we show that regular and chaotic trajectories exhibit different finite-time behavior despite the convergence of $\Omega$ in both regimes. For quasiperiodic trajectories with Diophantine frequency vectors, deviations from the limiting average decay as $\mathcal{O}(\tau^{-1})$, whereas sufficiently mixing chaotic dynamics exhibit root-mean-square fluctuations of order $\tau^{-1/2}$ under suitable correlation assumptions. This difference in finite-time convergence and fluctuation scaling provides the theoretical basis for using $\Omega$ to discriminate between the two dynamical regimes. We validate the proposed approach in the H\'enon--Heiles and Fermi--Pasta--Ulam systems, comparing the resulting classification of initial conditions with SALI as a reference chaos indicator. The results support $\Omega$ as a complementary single-trajectory diagnostic for chaos detection and as a practical source of scalar features for the analysis of trajectory ensembles, particularly in settings involving large numbers of trajectories or high-dimensional systems.
item.dc:creator: Javier Jim\'enez-L\'opez, V. J. Garc\'ia-Garrido

item.title: A zero-one law for the spectral gap property of pairs in SU(2)
item.description: arXiv:2603.17869v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $n \ge 2$, Gamburd, Jakobson, and Sarnak [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 1, 51-85 (1999)] conjectured that almost every $n$-tuple in $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ has a spectral gap. Toward this conjecture, Fisher [Int. Math. Res. Not. (2006)] established a zero-one law for $n \ge 3$, but obtained only a partial result for $n=2$. In this paper, we prove that the zero-one law also holds for $n=2$. We also remark that a Baire categorical analogue of this result holds.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Pikhurko, Kohki Sakamoto

item.title: Sofic measures
item.description: arXiv:2604.11212v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Sofic measures, also known as hidden Markov measures, have been extensively studied. In this paper, we survey some equivalent definitions of this notion and improve a bound for deciding whether a sofic measure is~$k$-step Markov. We prove that if an invariant sofic measure with a linear representation of dimension~$n$ is a~$k$-step Markov chain, then~$k$ can be chosen at most equal to~$\binom{n}{2}$ and that this bound is tight for sofic measures over an alphabet of size $3$.
item.dc:creator: Marie-Pierre B\'eal, Vincent Jug\'e, Eugene Gilburg, Jean Mairesse, Dominique Perrin

item.title: Odd-even dichotomy in the waveforms of modified Emden oscillators of arbitrary integer power
item.description: arXiv:2608.09008v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Closed-form waveforms of the modified Emden oscillators $\ddot x+(q+2)kx^q\dot x+k^2x^{2q+1}+\omega^2x=0$ of arbitrary natural power $q$, and of their damped $c$-deformed versions, are obtained through a generalized commutative factorization that reduces them to Bernoulli equations. We show that commutative factorizations of Li\'enard equations are gauge-conjugated forms of the nonlocal linearizing transformation of Chandrasekar, Senthilvelan, Kundu and Lakshmanan, the factorization constant being half the difference of the roots of the associated linear oscillator. These oscillators display an odd--even dichotomy: for odd $q$ they are isochronous, with period $2\pi/\omega$ independent of the amplitude, within an explicitly bounded range of the integration constant, while for even $q$ the oscillations decay algebraically, as $t^{-1/q}$. The dichotomy is confirmed by an elliptic polar representation, in which the phase rotates uniformly for every $q$, and, for even $q$, by the Bendixson--Dulac criterion applied to the divergence of the vector field. We present a dissipative Lagrangian of Lurie--Rayleigh type and, for $q=1$, an autonomous Sundman linearization that yields a rational first integral, a Jacobi last multiplier and a non-dissipative Lagrangian; for every $q$, $\omega^2x^2+(\dot x+kx^{q+1})^2$ is a Darboux polynomial providing a global Jacobi last multiplier. Explicit waveforms and phase portraits are given for $q=1,\dots,4$, with and without damping, and a recent application to magnon dynamics in the magnetic semiconductor CrSBr is discussed.
item.dc:creator: J. de la Cruz, H. C. Rosu

item.title: Ziggurats, taut foliations, and contact structures
item.description: arXiv:2608.30031v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the geography of taut foliations on compact $3$-manifolds with toroidal boundary components. The central object of our work is the set of boundary multislopes realized by foliations transverse to a fixed flow on such a manifold. We prove that these sets exhibit remarkable structural properties (rationality, rigidity, and convexity) which motivate the name ziggurats. Our main tool, of independent interest, is a two-way correspondence between foliations and contact structures on $3$-manifolds with boundary: we generalize the Eliashberg-Thurston theorem, which produces pairs of positive and negative contact structures from foliations, and a construction of the first author, which builds foliations from such contact pairs. Using both directions of this correspondence, we bring contact-geometric methods to bear on the architecture of ziggurats.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Massoni, Jonathan Zung

item.title: Effective Joint Equidistribution of Subspaces of Bounded Height in Rigid Adelic Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2608.30608v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an effective joint equidistribution theorem for $d$-dimensional $K$-subspaces, $1\le d<n$, of a fixed $n$-dimensional rigid adelic space over a number field $K$. The parameters are the height, the image in the archimedean Grassmannian, and the isometry classes of the subspace and quotient after each is rescaled to height $1$. For bounded Lipschitz test functions, the error term is power-saving with an explicit exponent. As an application, our theorem refines Thunder's asymptotic formula for subspaces of bounded height. We also obtain a power-saving asymptotic for subspaces containing $d$ linearly independent projective points of bounded height, with a leading constant expressed as a moment of the last successive minimum.
item.dc:creator: Ruida Di

item.title: Same path, different walk: a mechanistic comparison of looped and stacked transformer encoders on 12-lead ECG
item.description: arXiv:2609.15498v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Recurrent Transformers reusing their weights rather than stacking $L$ distinct layers are becoming widely adopted due to their parameter efficiency [1,2,3]. However, the exact representational and dynamical differences between looped and stacked architectures remain uncharacterized. This paper presents a controlled study on the example of bViT model [1] applying one weight-tied block $L$ times. We train two models: bViT and standard ViT [4] on 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) classification tasks from the PTB-XL dataset under identical training protocols. Despite an $8.9\times$ parameter reduction, bViT achieves accuracy parity with ViT. Geometric similarity metrics demonstrate that both architectures construct comparable latent representations in an equivalent canonical order. Crucially, their dynamics differ: bViT exhibits smaller step sizes and inter-patient sensitivity, as well as near-neutral behavior away from the data manifold, whereas ViT exhibits collapsing dimensionality of representations and out-of-distribution feature expansion.
item.dc:creator: Pawel Olszowiec, Michal Byra, Grzegorz Gruszczynski, Grzegorz Stefanski, Alberto Presta

item.title: What remains when integrability fails? Mathematical structure in the K(m,m) compacton equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.17489v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Peter Lax's 1968 discovery that certain nonlinear wave equations possess operator pairs (Lax pairs) opened the theory of completely integrable systems, yielding exact solutions, infinite conservation hierarchies, and perfectly elastic soliton collisions. When a nonlinear dispersive equation is provably non-integrable (admitting no Lax pair and only finitely many conservation laws), what mathematical structure governs its dynamics? The K(m,m) compacton equations, u_t + (u^m)_x + (u^m)_{xxx} = 0 for m >= 2, provide a testing ground: they support traveling waves with compact support, yet fail every known integrability test. We prove universal algebraic formulas determining the shape, width, and speed of every K(m,m) compacton. We develop a constraint-deficit mechanism explaining how the five independent conservation laws constrain emergent amplitudes and suppress the fundamental Fourier mode of the collision debris, while higher radiation modes remain unconstrained. The mechanism's conclusions rest on explicit hypotheses supported by numerical evidence. A phase-plane analysis reveals the compacton as a singular limit of smooth solitary waves through simultaneous regularity loss and support compactification. These results delineate intermediate territory between integrable order and generic nonlinear dynamics, organized by scaling universality and by the constraint deficit of a finite conservation structure.
item.dc:creator: James M. Hyman

item.title: Theoretical and Computational Advances in Birkhoff Pseudospectral Transcription for Aerospace Optimal Control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17842v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Birkhoff pseudospectral methods replace the differentiation matrices of classical transcriptions with integration operators whose conditioning does not deteriorate with polynomial order. This paper presents theoretical and computational advancements toward their practical use in aerospace optimal control. The initial-point-anchored Birkhoff integration operator is constructed explicitly for flipped Legendre-Gauss-Radau grids and related exactly to the corresponding Lagrange differentiation matrix and, through a reflection, to the standard Radau Birkhoff operator, whose conditioning properties it inherits. Rate constraints on nonlinear functions of states and controls are enforced directly through the pseudospectral operators and, for control-rate limits, shown to be primal and dual equivalent to state augmentation. Non-affine time mappings concentrate the nodes around localized trajectory features, and composing affine scaling and equilibration transformations provides a systematic way to construct scaling strategies. The methods are implemented in the open-source MATLAB framework RAPTOR and tested across a range of challenging optimal control problems, including a dense-grid orbit-raising problem, a rate-limited landing scenario, a Space Shuttle entry problem, and a five-phase reusable-launch-vehicle mission.
item.dc:creator: Riccardo Minnozzi, Marco Sagliano

item.title: Drift and joint minimal displacement for groups acting on hyperbolic spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.19787v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We obtain a uniform lower bound for the drift of random walks on hyperbolic spaces in terms of joint minimal displacement. Our main theorem applies to weakly acylindrical actions on Gromov-hyperbolic spaces and is quantitative in all relevant constants. For discrete isometry groups of Hadamard manifolds with pinched negative curvature, the required assumptions are automatically satisfied by the Margulis lemma. This yields uniform gaps at zero in drift spectra for pinched negatively curved Hadamard manifolds, hyperbolic groups, and mapping class groups acting on curve graphs.
item.dc:creator: Koji Fujiwara, Ryokichi Tanaka

item.title: The role of distributed friction dynamics on heave-induced motion of offshore drilling systems: modelling, analysis, and simulations
item.description: arXiv:2610.22189v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper investigates the influence of friction dynamics on heave-induced disturbance propagation using a coupled hydraulic-structural drilling model formulated as a semilinear interconnection of ordinary and hyperbolic partial differential equations (ODE-PDEs), and capturing spatially distributed memory effects in the drillstring-wellbore interaction. First, local and global existence and uniqueness results are established, and sufficient conditions for boundedness and input-to-state stability are deduced via a small-gain analysis. Subsequently, extensive numerical investigations are carried out, including harmonic excitation studies, nonlinear distortion analysis, spatial amplification investigations, mechanism-isolation experiments, parameter sensitivity analysis, and broadband simulations under realistic offshore sea-state excitation. The simulation results indicate that, whilst the hydraulic response is governed primarily by wave propagation phenomena, compressibility, and boundary reflections, the structural dynamics display substantially greater sensitivity to distributed friction effects. Furthermore, drillstring-wellbore friction is shown to have a relatively limited influence on well-posedness but a potentially significant impact on stability margins. These findings highlight the importance of accounting for coupled hydraulic-structural dynamics and distributed friction mechanisms when analysing, monitoring, and controlling offshore drilling systems.
item.dc:creator: Luigi Romano, Ole Morten Aamo
